notes: encoding::xml: Go's tokenizer (byte-exact errors, line numbers and offsets, name spaces, Strict/AutoClose/Entity/CharsetReader), Encoder and struct-tag Marshal/Unmarshal through the Marshal/Unmarshal traits and the rust-stdlib-derive macros. Documented differences: float digits are chosen by Rust's shortest formatter with ties resolved like Go; type strings in error messages are Rust type names; invalid UTF-8 bytes inside names show as U+FFFD; Decoder recursion is bounded by a stack budget (max_unmarshal_stack, default 1 MiB) as well as Go's depth limit, because it recurses on the native thread stack

Decoder.CharsetReader.note: Option<Box<dyn FnMut(&str, Box<dyn Read>) -> Result<Box<dyn Read>, Box<dyn Error>>>>; the input is the remaining stream

Decoder.Decode.note: decode returns a new value; decode_into fills an existing one. Unmarshal recurses on the native thread stack, which is fixed-size in Rust (Go's grows on demand). Measured about 800 bytes per nesting level in release and over 6 KiB in debug, so Go's 10000 levels overflow a default 2 MiB or 8 MiB stack. Decoder::max_unmarshal_stack (default 1 MiB) turns that into the 'exceeded max depth' error instead of an abort; raise it together with the thread's stack size to decode the full max_unmarshal_depth of 10000 (tested with a 1 GiB stack).

Decoder.DecodeElement.note: start is Option<&StartElement>; decode_element returns a new value and decode_element_into fills an existing one

Decoder.Entity.note: HashMap<String, String>; xml::html_entity() builds Go's HTMLEntity map

Decoder.RawToken.note: Result<Token, Error>; end of input is Err(Error::Eof)

Decoder.Token.note: Result<Token, Error>; end of input is Err(Error::Eof)

Encoder.Encode.note: generic over the Marshal trait instead of reflection

Encoder.EncodeToken.note: Token is an enum; Go's invalid-token-type errors cannot occur

HTMLAutoClose.note: html_auto_close() returns it as the Vec<String> Decoder::auto_close takes

HTMLEntity.note: sorted table; html_entity() returns the HashMap Decoder::entity takes

Marshal.note: generic over the Marshal trait; the derive (rust-stdlib-derive) reads Go's xml struct tags

NewTokenDecoder.note: Always wraps the argument; Go returns an existing *Decoder unchanged, so its settings and state are shared rather than wrapped.

SyntaxError.Error.note: An invalid UTF-8 byte inside a reported name appears as U+FFFD in the message; Go prints the raw byte.

TagPathError.Error.note: the Display impl gives Go's Error() text; checked by tools/xml_check.py

TagPathError.Struct.note: the struct's type name as a string instead of a reflect.Type

Token.note: enum of StartElement, EndElement, CharData, Comment, ProcInst, Directive

Unmarshal.note: Error texts name Rust types (type_name) where Go prints reflect.Type strings such as main.T; inexpressible. unmarshal returns a new value; unmarshal_into decodes into an existing one (Go's Unmarshal(data, &v)).

UnmarshalError.Error.note: the Display impl gives Go's Error() text; checked by tools/xml_check.py

UnsupportedTypeError.Error.note: the Display impl gives Go's Error() text; checked by tools/xml_check.py

UnsupportedTypeError.Type.note: the type's name as a string instead of a reflect.Type
